samples.summary:
None of the design doc's Goals are delivered: the whole feature is gated on an upstream release that does not exist, so it ships unreachable for every user.

`MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` but `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `@yorkie-js/react: "0.7.22"`, so `supportsClientKey()` is false on every build produced by this branch. That predicate gates the durable client (`use-durable-document.ts`), `OfflineRuntime`'s mount in `PrivateRoute.tsx`, the Settings switch (`app/settings/page.tsx`), and the chip's offer — so no store is ever attached, `saved-locally` is unreachable, and neither opt-in entry point renders.

The design doc's own Rollout framed PR 4 as a dark launch on the grounds that "nothing changes for anyone **until they opt in**", which presumes opting in is possible. The added Status section concedes it is not: "no Goal below is delivered until the dependency is bumped." So the stated outcome — "edits made while disconnected survive a reload" — works for nobody, and ~4,000 lines of storage, election, erase and recovery machinery land with no ship date inside this repo's control. The gate itself is the right safety call; the finding is that the change cannot satisfy its own acceptance criteria as merged.
samples.evidence: yorkie-capabilities.ts: `export const MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23";` vs package.json `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`. docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Status: "That release does not exist yet ... no Goal below is delivered until the dependency is bumped."

samples.summary:
The change bundles PRs 2–5 of its own Rollout table into a single diff, defeating the separation the doc gives a reason for.

The Rollout section states: "The structural change and the behavior change land separately, so that a regression in either is unambiguous", and specifies PR 3 as "per-document client, app lock, fallback — **still passing no store**. Structure only". This diff lands PR 2 (`wafflebase-doc-store.ts`), PR 3 (`durable-session.ts`, `use-durable-document.ts`), PR 4 (the store wiring, Settings + chip opt-in, `durable` chip, `OfflineRuntime`, offline-copy recovery) and PR 5 (the `sync-status.md` revision) at once.

Cost is inside the codebase — a regression anywhere in the storage/election/erase/recovery surface is no longer attributable to one of four staged changes, which is exactly the property the doc wrote the table to buy.
samples.evidence: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Rollout, PR rows 2–5, all present in this single diff.

samples.summary:
The design doc twice claims the recovery path reuses the existing copy engine; the implementation does not use it at all.

§ Losing work anyway: "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and § See Also: "[document-copy.md](document-copy.md) — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses".

`packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts` imports neither. It calls `createWorkspaceDocument` (`@/api/workspaces`) and then `applyImportedContent` (`@/app/documents/apply-imported-content`) — the *import* engine — plus a bespoke `writeNote`. That is arguably the correct choice, since `POST /documents/:id/copy` copies from a server-side source document and here the source is archived local bytes the server does not have; but the doc asserts a reuse relationship that does not exist, and a reader sent to `document-copy.md` to understand this path learns nothing about it. Either the two claims should name `applyImportedContent`, or the See Also link should point there.
samples.evidence: offline-copy-recovery.ts imports `createWorkspaceDocument`, `applyImportedContent`, `YorkieDocStore`, `YorkieSlidesStore`, `YorkieBoardStore`; no reference to `copyDocument` or `/documents/:id/copy` (confirmed by grep across packages/frontend/src).

samples.summary:
PR 5's revision of `sync-status.md` missed the section the change actually invalidates: the two exit guards are no longer the same condition.

§ The navigation guard still reads "So the **same condition, decided the same way**, also holds back in-app navigation" and "`SyncStatusChip` registers it next to the unload guard, which is what makes the coverage identical and free". § The unload guard still shows `const mayHaveUnsent = state === 'saving' || state === 'not-saved';` and "So the guard covers both".

This change splits them deliberately — `sync-status-chip.tsx` now computes `leavingLosesWork = mayHaveUnsent || savedLocally` for the navigation guard while `beforeunload` stays on `mayHaveUnsent`, and the nav guard's dialog copy branches on `savedLocally`. The revision updated the states table, the Non-Goals and the `SyncState` union but left the canonical description of the guard coupling stating the opposite of what ships. The offline doc explains the split under "Only `beforeunload`, though", but sync-status.md is the doc that owns these two sections.
samples.evidence: sync-status.md:246 `const mayHaveUnsent = state === 'saving' || state === 'not-saved';`; sync-status.md:279-282 "the same condition, decided the same way" / "coverage identical". Diff: sync-status-chip.tsx adds `const leavingLosesWork = mayHaveUnsent || savedLocally;` and passes it to `useNavigationGuard`.

samples.summary:
Two docs describe the feature in the past tense as delivered, when the version gate makes it observable by nobody.

`sync-status.md` Non-Goals: "~~**A user-facing offline mode toggle.**~~ **Shipped** as a per-*device* Settings preference, off by default." The `docs/design/README.md` row likewise describes the chip state, the opt-in and the `(offline copy)` recovery as characteristics of the system.

On the shipped `@yorkie-js/react@0.7.22` pin the Settings section is not rendered at all (`app/settings/page.tsx` wraps it in `offlineAvailable && …`), so "Shipped" is not true of any build. `offline-local-persistence.md` is honest about this in its Status section; the two documents a reader is most likely to reach first are not. Cost is documentation accuracy only, but the repo files design docs by validity and these two currently overstate it.
samples.evidence: sync-status.md: "Shipped as a per-*device* Settings preference"; app/settings/page.tsx: `{offlineAvailable && ( <section> … Offline … )}` where `offlineAvailable = supportsClientKey()`, false at the current pin.

samples.summary:
`writeNote` re-implements `applyImportedContent`'s Yorkie client lifecycle instead of extending that module with a `note` branch.

Its own comment concedes the relationship — "Mirrors `applyImportedContent`'s own lifecycle: `activate()` sits outside the `try` so an activation failure surfaces as itself rather than as a masking cleanup error" — and the two bodies are the same shape: construct `new Client({ rpcAddr, apiKey, authTokenInjector: fetchYorkieToken })`, `activate()`, attach a `Document` on the type-prefixed key, mutate, `detach`, `if (client.isActive()) deactivate()`.

`apply-imported-content.ts` already owns that lifecycle, the doc-key construction (`buildDocKey`) and the tested failure semantics (`__tests__/apply-imported-content.test.ts` has six cases pinning activate/deactivate ordering). A `note` arm there would have inherited all of it; as written there are now two copies of the client lifecycle to keep in step if the client options, retry behavior or auth injector ever change, and only one of them is covered by those six cases.
samples.evidence: offline-copy-recovery.ts:320-341 `writeNote` vs apply-imported-content.ts:233-308 — both construct `new Client({...})`, `await client.activate()` outside the try, and `if (client.isActive()) await client.deactivate()` in the finally.

samples.summary:
The recovery path changes the behavior of the shared Miro-import mapper, and no design doc records it.

`MappedInit` gains an `id` field, `handleOf()` falls back from `__id` to `id`, and the new `mapDescendants()` walks `data.children` recursively registering every descendant id into the handle map. These run for *every* caller of `applyBoardElements`, including the existing Miro import, not only for elements read back out of an archive.

The risk is bounded — `handleOf` prefers `__id`, so a mapper-produced init is unaffected — but `mapDescendants` now populates `realIds` with identity mappings for group children on the import path too, which it did not before. `offline-local-persistence.md` § Losing work anyway describes recovery as rehydrating through `Document.fromBytes()` and states "This requires no SDK change at all"; it does not mention that the import mapper had to change, so a reader of that doc would not know the Miro import shares the edit. A sentence in the design doc (or in the import's own doc) would make the coupling visible.
samples.evidence: apply-imported-content.ts: `type MappedInit = ElementInit & { __id?: string; id?: string };`, `function handleOf(element)` returning `element.__id ?? element.id`, and `mapDescendants(mapped, realIds)` called unconditionally in pass 1.

samples.summary:
Unrelated formatting churn inflates the diff.

`vite.config.ts` has one substantive change (the `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` define and the `frontendPkg` read) but is rewritten throughout from double to single quotes; `packages/frontend/src/lib/utils.ts` changes only quotes and semicolons; `components/__tests__/collab-document-provider.test.tsx` is requoted across ~40 lines around two real mock additions. Prettier is write-only here and no lane checks formatting, so this is reviewer cost rather than a lint failure — but it makes the substantive edits in those three files hard to pick out.
samples.evidence: vite.config.ts: ~60 quote-only line changes surrounding the `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` define; lib/utils.ts: the entire hunk is quote/semicolon only.

finding.evidence: yorkie-capabilities.ts: `export const MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23";` vs package.json `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`. docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md § Status: "That release does not exist yet ... no Goal below is delivered until the dependency is bumped."

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out against the repository. yorkie-capabilities.ts:24 declares MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"; vite.config.ts:414-418 injects __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__ straight from the frontend package.json pin, which is "@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22" (package.json:66, confirmed by pnpm-lock.yaml:5890). atLeast() (yorkie-capabilities.ts:44-57) is a strict x.y.z compare, so supportsClientKey() is false on every build this branch produces. That predicate gates the durable client (use-durable-document.ts:127-132), the provider branch (collab-document-provider.tsx:239), the chip's offer (sync-status-chip.tsx:117), the Settings switch (app/settings/page.tsx:42) and the OfflineRuntime mount (PrivateRoute.tsx:28-30, 58). The design doc itself concedes the consequence at docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:45-69 ("That release does not exist yet ... no Goal below is delivered until the dependency is bumped") and again in Rollout at :705-715, while the Goals at :71-83 include "Edits made while disconnected survive a reload". So the stated outcome is unreachable for every user as merged — an acceptance criterion left unmet, which is major and blocking under the design-fit rubric. The only inaccuracy is minor and does not change the conclusion: PrivateRoute mounts OfflineRuntime on supportsClientKey() OR a stored preference, but both preference-setting entry points are themselves behind the same gate, so no preference can be set on such a build. No guard, dependency override, or issue text was found that would open the gate or reframe an inert landing as the accepted criteria.
